source.author: Paulo José Martins Jorge da Silva
source.title: Portfolio Insurance Strategies: Friend or Foe?
source.treatment: Original Thai teaching synthesis with printed and PDF page citations; source PDF not redistributed.
source.numericExcerpt: Table 5.2 Panel C, printed page 90 / PDF page 117; two scenarios transcribed and checked visually. Values are cumulative prospect scores, not investment returns.

interactiveModels.dataType: Newly authored deterministic hypothetical returns; not market data or thesis replication
interactiveModels.cppi: Monthly rebalance, no leverage or shorts, fractional holdings, terminal floor target
benchmarks: Constant Mix 60% risky / 40% safe with monthly rebalancing
interactiveModels.costs: No transaction costs, bid-ask spread, slippage, taxes or dividends
interactiveModels.protectivePut: One asset and one European put, held to expiry; hypothetical premium; no option pricing model
interactiveModels.limitations: No probability or forecasting claim; monthly observations omit intramonth losses; model does not include market impact, liquidity constraints or counterparty failure

presentation.format: Thai book with sequential chapter and inline experiments

teachingExpansion.scope: Expanded all 13 existing sections; retained anchors and the three original interactive models.
newExamples: Four CPPI rebalancing periods and a round-trip path
Continuous unconstrained CPPI derivation, separate from the monthly model
Gap thresholds with interest and capped exposure
EUT certainty equivalent and cumulative prospect weights
teachingExpansion.reproducibility: 36 Notebook cells, including 17 executed code cells; prose and equations copied from canonical chapter; analytic assertions and 16 Python/JavaScript path comparisons.
teachingExpansion.sourceTreatment: New examples and derivations are teaching additions, not thesis tables or a replication. Thesis findings retain printed/PDF page references; Table 5.2 Panel C was checked visually.

teachingFigures.authoring: Editable Excalidraw primitives; validated with excalidraw skill; no external upload
teachingFigures.export: scripts/export_diagrams.py reads the scenes and embeds the existing licensed project fonts in SVG
teachingFigures.assumptions: Hypothetical lesson examples, monetary units, initial value 100, floor 90, multiplier 3, zero interest/costs, fractional holdings, no leverage/shorts; TIPP protects 90% of observed own-portfolio high-water mark
teachingFigures.limits: No optimal multiplier claim or market-data claim. Gap risk can breach the target. TIPP observations are not a continuous guarantee.
teachingFigures.notebook: Four SVGs embedded verbatim as Markdown attachments; no companion images needed

variableMultiplierExtension.source: Antje Mahayni (2013), joint work with D. Zieling and S. Balder, Performance evaluation of optimized portfolio insurance strategies, slides 3 and 9–12
variableMultiplierExtension.example: Original teaching rule: clamp(3 * 0.20 / positive estimated annual volatility, 1, 6); initial wealth 100, floor 90, zero rate/costs, no borrowing/shorts
variableMultiplierExtension.scope: Worked prose and executable Notebook; existing browser lab remains fixed-m CPPI; no empirical performance or optimality claim

source.provider: S&P Dow Jones Indices via FRED, SP500
source.measure: Daily close price index, no dividends; input kept local

assumptions.reset: Each calendar year independently; previous year final trading close to current year final close
assumptions.signal_lag: All volatility estimates end one trading close before execution
assumptions.execution: Idealized observed closing prices; no intraday stop fills; fractional holdings
assumptions.obpi: Reserve 90 + European ATM calls, r=q=0; start trailing 252-return volatility fixed through expiry; theoretical premiums and marks, not traded option history

sp500HistoricalTest.scope: Derived annual statistics for five insurance rules plus Buy & Hold; raw index observations remain local; OBPI is a theoretical-price illustration, not a traded-options backtest

charts.scope: Four strategy versus Buy & Hold daily wealth charts, excluding options; annual experiments compounded, annual floor/allocation renewal; 2012 points including inception. Desktop/mobile SVG exports; full-size charts embedded in Notebook.
